observations.title: iroh 1.5.0 (fork): no measurable change in outcomes, RTT, throughput, bind times or connection stability
observations.detail: Every scenario whose environment did not change keeps its direct/relay outcome; no connection was lost (0 disconnect events in 93 peer runs), QUIC counters in 93/93, every run reported. Lab: RTT 40.4 / 80.6 ms direct / relayed and throughput ~123 / ~35 Mbps as in campaigns 1-4, connect and hole-punching times identical (130 / 217-243 / 290-305 ms), bind 608-609 ms (3.2 s with UDP blocked), idle and NAT-flush survival 9/9 with 41 ms recovery. The lab's own relay ran iroh-relay 1.5.0 (relayed RTT, throughput and relay_compare unchanged); the real relay stayed on 1.4.1 and carried the 1.5.0 clients without drops. Real-world RTT 34-38 ms in the two route clusters, direct transfers 131-150 Mbps (campaign 4: 131-147 apart from its slow runs), relayed 76-78 Mbps. Verdicts: 110 right / 1 misleading / 0 wrong runs, as in campaigns 3 and 4.

observations.title: Outcome changes rw-symmetric-to-ufw, rw-ufw-to-easy, rw-ufw-to-symmetric (relay -> direct) are this machine's firewall, not iroh
observations.detail: The build machine was reinstalled on 2026-11-11 and has run without ufw since. The *-ufw scenarios used a random UDP port that ufw dropped (default deny inbound); campaign 4 relayed these three and reached rw-easy-to-ufw's direct path only after the relay. Now all four go direct (60 direct / 33 relay final paths, was 51 / 42). Control: debug/ufw-emul ran the four scenarios 3 times each with the same 1.5.0 binary, the local node on a fixed port (56095) and an nftables rule dropping new inbound UDP to it (what ufw did; replies to packets the node sent pass): rw-easy-to-ufw relay first then direct after 142-149 ms in 3/3, the other three relay only in 3/3, i.e. exactly campaign 4's outcomes. The verdict checks follow (254 -> 251: the relay_reason checks of the nine runs that are direct now became healthy_direct checks).

observations.title: New ERROR/WARN lines at every few endpoint shutdowns (iroh fork's relay-recovery commit, harmless)
observations.detail: 84 of the campaign's 204 .err files (bench and listen, lab, real world, startup and relay: 41 % of process exits) end with `ERROR iroh::socket::transports::relay: relay_recv_channel closed` (several), `WARN iroh::socket::transports: All transports failed to receive. QUIC endpoint will be shutdown.` and `ERROR noq::endpoint: I/O error: All transports failed to receive`; campaign 4 had none. All of them come between -0.2 ms and +0.9 s of the process's last event (the bench_report, or the listener's final disconnect), i.e. during Endpoint::close; no run lost a connection or a report. Local repro (debug/shutdown-logs: a local relay and directory, 10 local checks and 10 listen/bench pairs per build): golem-p2p with iroh 1.4.1 (crates.io) 0 of 30 processes, with upstream iroh main 2c12bb58 (1.5.0 without the fork's commit) 0 of 30, with the fork rev 4ad24ac2 7 of 30. So it comes from the relay-recovery commit: at shutdown its relay actors no longer wait for the graceful WebSocket close (close_relay_sink is cancelled by the stop token), so they drop the datagram channel while the QUIC endpoint still polls the relay transport, whose poll_recv logs a closed channel at ERROR level. Not a golem-p2p bug; it should be fixed in the fork/upstream PR (e.g. treat the closed channel as shutdown, at debug level, or stop polling before the relay actor ends). Users and journald see ERROR lines on a normal stop until then.

observations.title: Lossy link: one upload count given up too early (bench bug, fixed in cda49ae); otherwise as in campaign 4
observations.detail: 13 runs (3 campaign + 10 debug/lossy-extra): packet_loss hint 9/13 (campaign 4: 9/13; the misses lost 0 of 113-119 packets, sampling), loss counting settled 13/13, relay_compare ok 13/13, concurrency throughput measured 13/13 (0.66-3.00 Mbps, median 0.99; campaign 4: 0.46-3.64, 0.95), 1 restart (debug run 7; campaign 4: 2), and in 2 runs the phase went on past half the time because its requests were about to finish (097e446). Healthy/exit 0 in 12/13: debug/lossy-extra run 5 failed its upload with no_count ('sent the whole upload, but the listener did not report what it received within 6 s', exit 5, verdict degraded): writing ended about 6.8 s in, the bench waited as long again for the count (count_wait: as long as the upload took) and gave up 13.6 s after the start, and the listener had all 10,000,000 bytes 0.9 s later (listen.jsonl: sink, ms 14,399). At least 8.75 MB had arrived in the first 6.8 s (flow control keeps writing within one 1.25 MB stream window of what arrived); the rest took over 7.7 s more. The wait assumed the last window drains about as fast as the upload went. Fixed after the campaign (cda49ae): the wait for an upload's count goes on while the listener still acknowledges data (the connection's received bytes grew in the last 3 s), up to the existing 30 s cap; tested with links that deliver after the base wait, stop delivering, or never answer. The campaign binary does not have the fix.

observations.title: Cut-off concurrency requests are cancelled on the wire now (campaign 4's bug, fixed in a08d715)
observations.detail: On the lossy link, concurrency requests reached the listener after the phase had ended in 2 of 13 runs (4 requests, at most 0.1 s later: in flight at the cut-off); campaign 4: 7 of 13 runs, 48 requests, up to 3.9 s later. After debug/lossy-extra run 7's restart the cut-off requests no longer used the uplink (it counted 1.06 Mbps; campaign 4's run 8: 0.46).

observations.title: No slow Hetzner -> lab downloads this time
observations.detail: All 24 direct real-world runs ran at 131-150 Mbps both ways (concurrency 252-334 Mbps). Campaign 4 had 3 slow runs (13.7-15.6 Mbps down) while this machine's load was 36-45; campaigns 1 and 3 had 1 and 2. This campaign ran on an idle machine (load < 0.4), which fits, but does not prove, CPU contention as the cause.

observations.title: Fast-path concurrency slightly higher
observations.detail: Lab direct concurrency 200-269 Mbps (median 236) over 33 runs, campaign 4 185-252 (219); relayed 75-79 (77, unchanged); real-world direct 252-334 (298). The phase takes 250-340 ms on these paths, so single runs vary by ~20 %; the shift is within that spread and not attributed (the data path, noq, is the same version). Not a regression.

observations.title: Harness: listener_saw was lost since 9e7afee (fixed in ff6fcd1)
observations.detail: 9e7afee moved listen's per-request lines ('request from .. via PATH') to debug level; lab.sh pair/matrix/listen and realworld.sh count them for listener_saw, which would have been '-' in the real-world re-run. lab.sh and realworld.sh now start listeners without --json with RUST_LOG=warn,golem_p2p=info,golem_p2p::listen=debug (GPL_LISTEN_LOG). The campaign itself is not affected (its listeners use --json events).

observations.title: The real relay is not a bottleneck at the tested load (unchanged)
observations.detail: Relay-only Hetzner -> p2p-relay1 -> Hetzner with 1.5.0 clients and the 1.4.1 relay: 39-42.5 Mbps per 4 MB transfer alone, ~40 Mbps each with 2 and with 4 at once (157-162 Mbps aggregate), no packets dropped.

limitations: Not every difference to campaign 4 is iroh's: the CLI and library changed in 30 commits since campaign 4 (closed networks with registry and membership certificates, security fixes such as bounded handshakes and registry answers, stricter certificate and record parsing, store and listener fixes, and two bench changes, see bench_settings), and this machine was reinstalled without a firewall. The debug runs separate the ones that showed up (ufw-emul, shutdown-logs); everything else stayed the same, so no attribution was needed.

The lab's relay is 1.5.0, the real relay 1.4.1: relayed lab paths test 1.5.0 clients with a 1.5.0 relay, everything through p2p-relay1 1.5.0 clients with a 1.4.1 relay. A 1.5.0 public relay was not tested.
3 runs per scenario (4-8 for the parallel relay runs): percentiles over runs are rough. The lossy-link statistics come from 13 runs (3 campaign + 10 debug, not in summary.json).

The verdict classification is ours (summarize.py), per run by its worst finding. A transfer_failed issue is not checked against what the listener received; debug/lossy-extra run 5's is misleading (the listener got everything 0.9 s later), but debug runs are not classified.
The packet_loss window holds 108-145 packets: at 1 % random loss about one window in three shows no loss.
The lab NATs are Linux conntrack + nftables with port preservation; one relay per scenario, so hard_nat (two relays) was never exercised.
No rate limits in the lab and fixed transfer sizes (10 MB direct, 4 MB relayed): throughput numbers show slow start for those sizes, not capacity.
Real world: one location (Helsinki), no firewall on this machine any more (ufw emulated only in debug/ufw-emul), per-flow routes of ~34 or ~37.5 ms between puppet's host and Hetzner.
--idle cannot show NAT mapping expiry: iroh keeps every path alive every 5 s and the lab's shortest mapping timeout is 5 s.
QUIC loss is counted only for packets the bench node sent; IPv4 only inside the lab.
Runs were sequential, but puppet's host also carries other services (its testnet listener and public relay, idle); their load was not controlled.
